newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Ameritech confident of Belgacom growth.
newsitem.headline: Ameritech confident of Belgacom growth.

text.p: Ameritech Corp said on Thursday that 1996 revenue of Belgacom was growing faster than expected and forecast that the Belgian telecommunications firm would be Europe's best performing operator by the year 2000.

"We are performing ahead of plan here. We see an eight to nine percent growth in revenue (in 1996) while we had expected five to seven percent," said Herbert Hribar, managing director of Ameritech Europe.
State-controlled Belgacom is 49.9 percent owned by a consortium led by Ameritech. It also includes Singapore Telecom, Tele Danmark and three Belgian companies.
"We are confident Belgacom will be one of the best if not the best operator in Europe in three to four years," Hribar told a news conference to mark the opening of Ameritech's Europe office.
Hribar said 1996 bottom-line profit was developing in line with expectations. Profit growth was likely to be sustained in 1997 and "on plan or slightly above for the next three years".

Full-year 1995 group net profit rose 10.3 percent to 10.7 billion Belgian francs ($341.2 million). Consolidated turnover was 127.1 billion, up 8.6 percent. Group net profit rose 15 percent to 6.6 billion in the six months to June 30.
Walter Catlow, Ameritech's executive vice-president and president of Ameritech International, said Ameritech still aimed to raise its stake in Belgacom.
"Our position has always been with the government that we have an interest in increasing our ownership," Catlow said.
He said Belgium, currently with an average penetration of 43 lines per 100 population, could "easily" rise to 50 to 55 lines.
Catlow said Ameritech, which is also a strategic partner in Hungarian telecom firm Matav and has interests in most European countries,, has so far invested more than $2 billion in Europe.
The new office will be responsible for Ameritech's European operations, business development and strategy.
"With the rapid liberalisation and expansion of European telecommunications, Brussels is the right place for our office," Catlow said.
He welcomed competition for Belgacom's profitable Proximus GSM service from Belgo-French company Mobistar, which is owned 62 percent by France Telecom.
"I am very optimistic about the outcome of our competition with Mobistar," Catlow said.
"Yes there have been price cuts and Proximus has been meeting these price cuts, but the growth in the number of subscribers you will see over the next year will be astronimical," he said.
Proximus has nearly 400,000 subscribers. Mobistar has signed up 20,000 clients in the first six weeks since its launch.
